problem.title: Quota Window
problem.statementMarkdown: Return the shortest contiguous substring of `text` containing every character of `quota` with at least its multiplicity. Match characters exactly, including case. Ties choose the earliest substring. Return an empty string if quota is empty or no window exists.

examples.explanation: BCA is the earliest shortest substring containing A, B, and C.
aab supplies two a characters and one b.

attribution: Original Quorem statement and fixture corpus, authored for this project.

approaches.explanationMarkdown: Maintain character deficits and the total number still missing. Expand the right boundary until the quota is met, then shrink the left boundary while it remains met. Update the best only for a strictly shorter window, preserving the earliest tie.
approaches.complexityNotes:
n and m count text/quota codepoints; k is the number of distinct quota characters. Each boundary crosses each character at most once; result storage is excluded.

Java: Time O(n + m); auxiliary space O(n + m). n and m count text/quota codepoints. This implementation retains character buffers and counts while preserving Unicode characters; result storage is excluded.
